Which ancient Indus Valley city, one of the largest urban centers of its civilization, is believed to have been rebuilt seven times as a result of catastrophic flooding?
questions.explanation: Mohenjo-Daro, located in present-day Pakistan, was one of the most sophisticated cities of the ancient Indus Valley Civilization (c. 2500 BCE). Archaeological evidence suggests the city was rebuilt at least seven times, each time on top of flood debris left by the Indus River. This repeated reconstruction reflects both the city's vulnerability to flooding and the remarkable resilience and urban planning capabilities of its inhabitants.
